newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks mixed, sluggish trend to continue.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks mixed, sluggish trend to continue.

text.p: Croatian stocks were mixed in thin trade on Friday and market participants said the sluggish trend was likely to continue next week.
"Buyers are quite cautious," Velimir Zelimorski of Fima Brokerage told Reuters.
He said potential small investors were keeping a low profile, pending local elections due in mid April which might losen the ruling HDZ grip on power.
Investors are also waiting for more information on companies to be included in a voucher privatisation, which could launch new stocks to the market, he added.

A list of assets in 800 companies, featuring the hotels, leading food companies Podravka and Kras, electrical firms Koncar and Elka and shippers was released by the privatisation authorities earlier on Friday.
Five of 12 active issues fell, three rose and four were unchanged. Volume doubled to 6,283 shares but turnover shrank slightly to 2.5 million kuna.
Food concern Podravka took the spotlight as top gainer and the most active stock of the day.
It closed 12 kuna higher at 320 kuna after trading mixed in 302-330 kuna range on volume of 3,546 shares. Traders said its price was likely to remain stable with smaller fluctuations.
Confectioner Kras, which recently had to suspend its bonbon production because of a ban on sugar imports, slid 10 kuna to 485 kuna with 170 shares changing hands.
Fully-listed drugs company Pliva edged down 11 kuna to 440 with 810 shares sold.

Another blue chip Zagrebacka Banka, was flat at 1,900 kuna on a small volume of 36 units, after hitting an all-time-high at 1,913 kuna Wednesday. But it ended the week 30 kuna higher than last Friday.
Laguna, gaining 30 kuna to 1,450 on volume of 470 units, stood out as most active among five hoteliers.
But traders said hotel stocks were unduly neglected and cited Istrian Jadranturist and Istraturist and Suncani Hvar from the Dalmatian island of Hvar as the most interesting.
The island is one of the top tourist destinations on Croatian coast. But its main hotelier led the day's decliners, falling four kuna to 66 on volume of 653 units.
"Suncani Hvar is sold at 60 percent of its face value. This is unrealistic given the location of its hotels and the fact an airport is in works there," said Zelimo.
